The derivation in the proposed solution is fully correct:

1. Writing $\psi = \sqrt{\mathcal{P}}\,e^{iS/\hbar}$, the components of the Fubini–Study metric evaluate to:
   $$g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{1}{4}\mathbb{E}[\partial_\mu \ln \mathcal{P}\,\partial_\nu \ln \mathcal{P}] + \frac{1}{\hbar^2}\operatorname{Cov}(\partial_\mu S, \partial_\nu S).$$
2. Using the standard Madelung–Bohm velocity definitions $\pi_\mu = \frac{1}{m}\partial_\mu S$ and $u_\mu = \frac{\hbar}{2m}\partial_\mu \ln \mathcal{P}$, we have:
   $$\operatorname{Cov}(\partial_\mu S, \partial_\nu S) = m^2 \operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu, \pi_\nu),$$
   $$\frac{1}{4}\mathbb{E}[\partial_\mu \ln \mathcal{P}\,\partial_\nu \ln \mathcal{P}] = \frac{m^2}{\hbar^2}\operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu, u_\nu).$$
3. Factoring out $\frac{m^2}{\hbar^2}$ yields:
   $$g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{m^2}{\hbar^2}\Bigl[\operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu) + \operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu,u_\nu)\Bigr]_{\mathcal{P}},$$
   giving $C = \dfrac{m^2}{x^2}$ with $x = \hbar$.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
